title: Developer Experience Docs Playbook: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Site Ops, and Top Support Fixes
author: Maya Chen
summary: Playbook for writing and operating developer-facing documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and canonical fixes for the top support issues.
content:
Overview

This playbook defines standards, templates, and operational procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation at Redwood Inference. It covers SDK guides, quickstarts and templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and the canonical fixes for the most frequent support issues. The goal is consistent, high-quality, discoverable documentation that reduces time-to-value for external developers and internal integrators.

Audience
- SDK authors and maintainers
- Developer docs writers and technical writers
- Solutions engineers and support on-call
- Product managers and API owners

Scope
- Public-facing SDK guides (Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, Go)
- Quickstarts and template repos used in onboarding and tutorials
- API examples kept in sync with codegen and REST/SDK changes
- Docs site operating procedures (content lifecycle, publishing, rollback)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes maintained as runnable playbooks

Standards and Structure (all new docs must follow)
1) A short intro and one-line summary.
2) Audience and prerequisites.
3) Quickstart (copy/paste runnable example).
4) Reference section with configuration table(s).
5) Troubleshooting / FAQ (include canonical fixes).
6) Ownership and review history.
7) Related pages and links to SDK repos or code samples.

Content Style
- Use complete sentences and active voice.
- Favor small, focused pages (500-1,500 words) for quick discovery.
- Keep code examples minimal, runnable, and pinned to a tested commit or tag.
- Use plain-text CLI examples and JSON/YAML for configuration.

Templates and Filenames
- Filenames: lowercase with dashes, include year when appropriate, e.g. "developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-2026".
- Template header (copy into new pages): title, summary, audience, prerequisites, quickstart, reference, troubleshooting, ownership, changelog.

SDK Guides (structure & checklist)
- One guide per language. Sections: install, auth, basic usage, advanced configuration (retries, batching, streaming), test matrix and supported versions.
- Include a pinned SDK version and example install commands. Example:
Python:
  pip install redwood-inference==0.8.2

Example quick usage (Python):
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
resp = client.generate(model="redwood-2b", prompt="Write a short haiku about latency")
print(resp.text)

JavaScript (Node):
import Redwood from 'redwood-inference';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const resp = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-2b', prompt: 'Summarize the playbook in one paragraph' });
console.log(resp.text);

Quickstarts & Templates (recommended repo layout)
- Each quickstart has: README.md, Dockerfile (optional), environment example (.env.example), CI snippet, and a link to the exact SDK tag used.
- Example quickstart topics: chat integration, summarization pipeline, embeddings + vector DB example, streaming responses with server-sent events.
- Template checklist before publishing: CI green, security scan (snyk/ghas), license header, tested on recommended SDK versions.

API Examples (keeping examples correct and discoverable)
- Canonical examples live in the SDK repos and are mirrored to docs site via the docs CI.
- Always include both REST (curl) and SDK examples for common tasks: text-generation, chat (multi-turn), embeddings, and function/tool calling.
- Example curl snippet:
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-2b","prompt":"Translate to French: Hello world"}'

Docs Site Operating Procedures
- Authors: create docs in the docs repo branch named docs/<ticket>-<short-desc>.
- Pull request checklist: content, code blocks tested, accessibility check, reviewer from docs team, reviewer from owning SDK team.
- Publishing: merge to main triggers staging build; QA reviewer signs off; use the release tag docs-site/vX.Y for production deploys.
- Rollback: revert PR and redeploy; notify #docs and #devex Slack channels and update page changelog.
- Versioning: clearly note API-breaking changes and add a compatibility table at top of pages.

Ownership and SLAs
- Each SDK guide and quickstart must list an owner (person and team) and a fallback (team page). Example ownership line: "Owner: Maya Chen (eng-developer-experience); Fallback: devex-oncall@redwood.ai".
- Docs SLO: Critical quickstarts (top-10 pages by traffic) must be reviewed quarterly. Broken-code alerts (docs CI) must be acknowledged within 24 hours by owner.

Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (2025-2026)
1) Auth failures: "invalid_api_key" in curl or SDK. Canonical fix:
- Verify REDWOOD_API_KEY set: echo $REDWOOD_API_KEY
- Ensure API key has the required scope in the Console (Keys -> Scopes)
- Example resolution command: 
  export REDWOOD_API_KEY="sk_live_..."
  curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
2) Streaming truncated responses in Node server (SSE/HTTP chunking). Canonical fix:
- Ensure server framework doesn't buffer responses (set res.flushHeaders() in Express), use recommended SDK streaming helper: client.stream({ ... }).
- Example Express snippet: res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream' }); res.flushHeaders();
3) High latency for short requests (cold start on private deployments). Canonical fix:
- Use warmup probe: POST /internal/warmup?model=redwood-2b at 60s intervals; enable persistent workers in deployment config.
4) Embedding quality regressions after model pin changes. Canonical fix:
- Run eval harness: scripts/evals/embeddings_regression_check.py --baseline-tag v2025-12-01 --candidate-tag v2026-01-01; pin model in customer config if needed.
5) Large-batch OOM errors on dedicated pools. Canonical fix:
- Reduce batch size to recommended for model/device; set dynamic_batching.max_tokens and per-worker memory_limit_mb in the route config; sample YAML: 
route_config:
  model: redwood-8b-quant
  dynamic_batching:
    max_tokens: "2048"
    max_batch_size: "8"
  worker:
    memory_limit_mb: "65000"

Troubleshooting Process (for support engineers)
1) Reproduce the issue with the customer's configuration in a sandbox.
2) Capture logs: request id, route, model, SDK version, exact payload.
3) If code example fails, run canonical example from this playbook and compare.
4) Escalate to runtime team if logs show kernel OOM or scheduling errors.
5) Document fix and add a short postmortem to the "regression-triage" folder if systemic.

Maintenance and Review Cadence
- Quarterly review for top-100 pages by traffic. Owners must run examples, update SDK versions, and sign off.
- Minor updates (typo, small clarifications) can be applied directly with one reviewer.
- Major updates (API/behavior changes) require an ADR and cross-team review.

Analytics and Measurement
- Track page traffic, example-run failures (docs CI), and support tickets routed from docs links. Target: reduce docs-originating support tickets by 30% year-over-year.

Related Resources
- Templates & quickstarts repo: github.com/redwood-inference/devex-quickstarts
- SDK repos: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-python-sdk, /redwood-js-sdk
- Eval harness: confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/eval-harness
